subject: math
title: Halves and Fourths
seo_title: Grade 1 Halves and Fourths Worksheets: Equal Shares and Quarters (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 halves and fourths worksheets with pictures of circles and rectangles: equal or not equal shares, halves, fourths and quarters, what part is shaded, and why a half is bigger than a fourth. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: 2 equal shares are halves. 4 equal shares are fourths, or quarters.
key_sub: The shares must be the same size. The whole is two halves or four fourths. More shares means smaller shares, so a half is bigger than a fourth.
body_html:
Equal shares

To share fairly, cut a shape into equal shares. Equal shares are all the same size.

Halves

2 equal shares are halves. Each share is half of the shape.

Fourths and quarters

4 equal shares are fourths. They are also called quarters. A fourth of a shape and a quarter of a shape are the same.

Equal sharesNameOne shareThe whole
2halveshalf oftwo halves
4fourths or quartersa fourth of, a quarter offour fourths

The whole

All the shares together make the whole.

More shares, smaller shares

Cut the same shape into more shares, and each share gets smaller.

Example

Ava shares a sandwich fairly with 3 friends. What share does each person get?

Ava and 3 friends are 4 people. 4 equal shares are fourths.

Answer: a fourth (a quarter) of the sandwich

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling 2 pieces halves when they are not the same sizeCheck that the shares are equal first
Thinking a fourth is bigger than a half because 4 is more than 2More shares means smaller shares. A half is bigger
Counting the lines instead of the sharesCount the shares: 2 lines can make 4 shares
Calling 4 equal shares halves4 equal shares are fourths. 2 equal shares are halves

faq.q: What are halves and fourths in 1st grade math?
faq.a: Halves are 2 equal shares of a shape. Fourths are 4 equal shares of a shape. First graders cut circles and rectangles into halves and fourths.

faq.q: Is a fourth bigger than a half?
faq.a: No. When the same shape is cut into more shares, each share is smaller. Half of a pizza is bigger than a fourth of the same pizza.

faq.q: Is a fourth the same as a quarter?
faq.a: Yes. A fourth and a quarter both mean 1 of 4 equal shares. 4 fourths, or 4 quarters, make 1 whole.
Equal shares are pieces of a shape that are all the same size. If one piece is bigger, the pieces are not halves or fourths.

items.q: A shape has 2 pieces. One piece is big. One piece is small. Are they halves?

items.q: Ella cuts a cookie in half. How many pieces does she have?

items.q: Max cuts a pancake into halves. He eats one half. How much is left?

items.q: Which is not a way to cut a rectangle in half?

items.q: Which is bigger: a fourth of a pizza or a quarter of the same pizza?

items.q: How many fourths make a whole?
items.e: Fourths are 4 equal shares. 4 fourths make a whole.

items.q: How many quarters make a whole?

items.q: What part of the circle is shaded?
items.e: All 4 fourths are shaded. 4 fourths make the whole circle.

items.q: How many more fourths must be shaded to shade the whole square?
items.e: The whole square is 4 fourths. 1 is shaded. 1 + 3 = 4, so 3 more must be shaded.

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: A is cut into halves. B is cut into fourths. A half is bigger than a fourth, so A is bigger. (4 is more than 2, but more shares means smaller shares.)

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: A is cut into fourths. B is cut into halves. A half is bigger than a fourth, so B is bigger.

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: Both squares are cut into fourths. Each shaded share is a fourth of the same square. A triangle and a small square can be the same size.

items.q: A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: Both squares are cut into halves. Half of a square is the same size, whether the cut goes down the middle or corner to corner.

items.q: The circles are the same size. Which circle has the smallest shares?
items.e: Circle C is cut into fourths. That is the most shares. More shares means smaller shares.

items.q: The rectangles are the same size. Which rectangle has the biggest shares?
items.e: Rectangle D is cut into halves. The others are cut into fourths. Fewer shares means bigger shares.

items.q: Which is bigger: half of a pizza or a fourth of the same pizza?
items.e: A half is 1 of 2 equal shares. A fourth is 1 of 4 equal shares. More shares means smaller shares. So half is bigger.

items.q: Which is smaller: a quarter of a cake or half of the same cake?
items.e: A quarter is 1 of 4 shares. Half is 1 of 2 shares. 4 shares are smaller, so a quarter is smaller.

items.q: You cut the same pie into more equal shares. What happens to each share?
items.e: The pie stays the same. More shares means each share is smaller.

items.q: Mia cuts her pancake into halves. Ben cuts the same size pancake into fourths. Whose pieces are bigger?
items.e: Ben has more pieces, so his pieces are smaller. Halves are bigger than fourths, so Mia’s pieces are bigger.

items.q: Ava shares a sandwich fairly with 3 friends. What share does each person get?
items.e: Ava and 3 friends are 4 people. 4 equal shares are fourths. Do not forget to count Ava.

items.q: Leo and his sister share a pizza fairly. What share does each one get?
items.e: Leo and his sister are 2 people. 2 equal shares are halves. Each one gets a half.

items.q: Four kids share a big cookie fairly. What share does each kid get?
items.e: Four kids means 4 equal shares. Each kid gets a quarter (a fourth) of the cookie.

items.q: Nora folds a paper in half. Then she opens it. How many equal shares does she see?
items.e: One fold makes 2 equal shares: 2 halves. The fold is 1 line, but it makes 2 shares.

items.q: Kai folds a square paper in half. He folds it in half again the other way. He opens it. What are the shares?
items.e: The 2 folds cross and make 4 equal shares. 4 equal shares are fourths.

items.q: Owen cuts a sandwich into 2 pieces. One is big and one is small. Did he cut it in half?
items.e: Halves must be the same size. A big piece and a small piece are not halves.

items.q: Ella gets half of an apple. Max gets a fourth of the same size apple. Who gets more?
items.e: Half is bigger than a fourth. So Ella gets more apple.

items.q: Omar is very hungry. Should he take half of a pie or a quarter of the same pie?
items.e: Half of a pie is bigger than a quarter of the same pie. Omar should take half.

items.q: Grace eats 2 halves of an orange. How much of the orange does she eat?
items.e: 2 halves make 1 whole. Grace eats the whole orange.

items.q: Lily cuts a square cake with 2 cuts. The cuts cross in the middle. How many equal shares are there?
items.e: 2 cuts that cross in the middle make 4 equal shares. Count the shares, not the cuts.
